speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy struggling with feeding and abdominal swelling. To understand what is going on, have you been vomiting, and if so, is it ever green or yellow?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: That tenderness is concerning. Has the baby had any episodes of passing gas or stool that look like currant jelly, and do you notice alternating periods of intense crying with a distended belly?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that history. Since there is no fever or classic bilious vomiting, is the stool currently normal in color, or does it look like pale clay? Also, did you notice any sudden onset of severe, paroxysmal crying spells that seemed to be relieved by passing gas?

text: Since the ultrasound is normal and we have ruled out mechanical obstruction like intussusception, is the baby passing any gas, and does the stool have a fruity or foul smell? Also, have you noticed any visible veins on the abdomen or a "sausage-shaped" mass upon gentle palpation?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.
